description: Site: oscal/emit.rs:256-266. EvidenceIndex::build deduplicates EvidenceKey using Vec::contains, which is O(n) per insertion → O(n^2) overall, where n = number of findings. Today (~50 RFC-conformance lints per cert, ~3 certs per chain) n is small and the cost is invisible. But the workspace's stated roadmap is pkix-policy-zlint adapting ~700 zlint checks, plus pkilint, plus custom lint bundles. A run against a typical CT log batch (10k certs × 100 lints each = 1M findings) hits O(1e12) comparisons. Fix: replace EvidenceKey-dedup Vec with HashSet<EvidenceKey> (EvidenceKey already derives Hash via Eq/PartialEq, but isn't actually Hash — it would need a derive). Keep the ordered Vec for output order, but skip Vec::contains in favor of HashSet::insert returning bool. O(n) overall. Net cost: one extra hash per finding, one extra HashSet allocation per report. Filed P2 because the present scale doesn't hurt; this is forward-looking.
title: EvidenceIndex::build is O(n*m) for evidence-key dedup, scales badly with zlint-grade rule sets
